subject: What's new in GiesChat: a weekly email about your agents
preheader: A weekly AI summary of your agents, plus course websites, newer models and more.
headline: A weekly email about your agents

intro.faculty: Here is what changed in GiesChat over the last two months and what it means for the agents you run for your classes.
intro.all: Here is what changed in GiesChat over the last two months. Items marked Faculty are for people who build agents for their classes.

clip.alt: Before and after: the Agent dashboard used to be the only place to see how agents were doing; now a Weekly email button lets you pick agents, people and a time, and each week an email arrives with the numbers and an AI summary for each agent.
clip.caption: Before: you had to open the dashboard to see how your agents were doing. After: a summary comes to your inbox every week.

changes.title: How the weekly email works
changes.body: On the Agent dashboard, click Weekly email and pick the agents you want to hear about and up to 10 Illinois addresses (yours is already filled in). Each week, at the day and time you choose (Friday 5 PM Central unless you change it), everyone on the list gets a short summary for each agent: conversations and students compared with the week before, a four-week trend, and a paragraph written by AI about what changed and what students asked. No student is named or quoted.

changes.title: Send yourself a test first
changes.body: Send me a test emails you a sample with made-up numbers right away, so you can see how it looks and confirm it reaches your inbox. If you don't see it within a few minutes, check your spam or junk folder, and mark GiesChat as a safe sender so the weekly email lands in your inbox.

changes.title: Your TAs' drafts keep up with your changes
changes.body: If you change an agent while a TA is working on a draft, they get a note and can bring their draft up to date in one step. Where you both edited the same thing, they see both versions and choose.

changes.title: Agents can learn from your course website
changes.body: In the agent builder, paste a course or department web address under Websites. GiesChat reads up to 50 pages from that site, saves a clean copy for your agent, and checks it again every night, so answers keep up when your site changes. If a site blocks GiesChat, it tells you and suggests uploading a PDF instead.

changes.title: More room for documents, and pictures count
changes.body: Agents built on the dashboard can now hold up to 100 documents, up from 50. Add a photo or screenshot of a table or chart and GiesChat reads the numbers into text, so students can ask about them.

changes.title: Run an agent inside your own course site
changes.body: If your course site has its own server, it can now send students' questions to one of your agents and show the answers on the page. Students sign in with their Illinois account, and those chats show up in GiesChat too. Click the key icon on an agent's row to create a key. The Agent API page in the GiesChat docs walks through the rest.

changes.title: Anyone can build an agent
changes.body: The class dashboard is now the Agent dashboard, and it is open to everyone with a GiesChat account, not just faculty. Build an agent there and see how people use it.

changes.title: Newer models
changes.body: Chat now runs on GPT-6 Luna. Class agents can also use GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet, Opus and Haiku 5.5.

changes.title: Fixed: editing an agent after opening its chat link
changes.body: Opening your own Illinois-only chat link no longer takes away your ability to edit that agent.
